A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same PISCES research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-P are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench experiments, a human preference study involving 400 prompts and 85 participants, and extensive appendix ablations and analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments, human preference results, qualitative comparisons, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The distributional OT map, partial-OT semantic alignment, dual rewards, and direct-backpropagation/GRPO procedures are unchanged. Algorithms 1-3 and the adaptive reward fusion in Appendix M are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebVid10M and VidGen-1M for short- and long-video post-training, retain VBench and VideoReward evaluation prompts, and include the same 100 out-of-distribution prompts in Appendix I.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the reported experiments. The IPO-to-Dual-IPO citation update and newly cited verifiable-rewards work do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain the same clip lengths, resolutions, training budgets, metrics, controls, and evaluation procedures, including the 400-prompt, 85-participant human study.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3-4.4 and Appendices D-O retain the same reward/component ablations, motion-guidance comparisons, evaluator and OOD tests, sensitivity analysis, failure example, reward-interaction analysis, and reward-hacking investigation.

E5.justification: Figure 3 error bars, Appendix J sweep variability, and Appendix L agreement and correlation statistics are unchanged. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 1 reports the same PISCES Total Scores of 82.75 for VideoCrafter2 and 85.45 for HunyuanVideo; appendix result tables and plots are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8 and the mathematical formulations in Appendices A-C are unchanged, including OT objectives, constraints, attention fusion, and training losses. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty and performance claims about annotation-free dual OT-aligned rewards, short- and long-video generation, and compatibility with multiple optimization strategies.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged, including the dependence on encoder precision in Appendix K, reward-hacking discussion in Appendix O, computational tradeoffs in Appendix P, and Impact Statement.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page address at the end of the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation details remain unchanged; the supplied PDFs do not establish that code or data have newly become available.

R1.justification: Section 2 newly acknowledges verifiable rewards as an annotation-free approach and cites Le et al. (2025b), 'What about gravity in video generation?'. This modestly broadens related-work coverage while retaining PISCES's existing novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 expands David Gu's displayed name, adds Mei Chen's current-affiliation note, replaces preprint information with conference publication details, and adds acknowledgments. Related-work wording and bibliography receive limited updates; the scientific exposition and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: The revised publication footnote, project-page line, and acknowledgments cause limited column and page reflow. Figures 1-10 and Tables 1-12 retain their content, captions, and designs; all six appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves documentation and context through the project-page pointer, funding acknowledgments, and recognition of verifiable-reward prior work in Section 2. The method, empirical evidence, and complete appendices remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
